findings.title: Dynamic !id! prefix underflow passes UINT_MAX into ReadSecMSG/OS_BF_Str before key auth.
findings.description: HandleSecureMessage strips !<id>! while decrementing recv_b, then calls ReadSecMSG(..., recv_b - 1) with an unsigned size. A frame that is exactly !<id>! leaves recv_b=0 so the size becomes 0xFFFFFFFF. The reused, non-NUL-terminated receive buffer retains a ':' from a prior !id!:ciphertext message at the strip offset, so ReadSecMSG proceeds into OS_BF_Str/BF_cbc_encrypt with that size and overflows stack cleartext_msg[OS_MAXSTR+1]. Only OS_IsAllowedDynamicID (agent id + IP/any) is required; the Blowfish key is never proven. Distinct from the known signed TCP length-prefix bug: this uses a valid positive UDP/TCP length equal to 2+len(id).
findings.impact: Remote stack buffer overflow in ossec-remoted (ossec user) on default secure remoted. Any network peer who can guess/learn an agent id with IP any (default authd without -i) or spoof a pinned agent IP can crash remoted and likely execute code, taking down secure event collection or yielding a foothold to read client.keys.
findings.attack_path:
1. Manager runs secure remoted (default).
2. An agent exists with IP any (authd without -i) or attacker can UDP-spoof a pinned agent IP.
3. Attacker learns/guesses the agent id.
4. Prior traffic or a prime packet leaves ':' at index 2+len(id) in remoted's receive buffer.
5. Attacker sends exactly !<id>! (UDP or TCP with length=2+len(id)).
6. ReadSecMSG decrypts with size UINT_MAX into a stack buffer → crash/RCE as ossec.
findings.remediation: After stripping !id!, require 1 <= remaining_len <= OS_MAXSTR before ReadSecMSG. Pass the remaining ciphertext length explicitly; do not compute recv_b-1 after mutating recv_b. NUL-terminate the receive buffer at recv_b. Cap OS_BF_Str to the cleartext buffer size.
findings.poc_video_notes: No live remoted lab. Local C replica of !id! accounting produced buffer_size=0xffffffff for !001!. Python leftover-buffer simulation showed prior !001!:... plus short !001! leaves ':' at the strip offset so the format check passes.

findings.title: Syslog-TCP remoted treats OS_RecvTCPBuffer success (0) as byte count, overflowing storage_buffer via strncat.
findings.description: OS_RecvTCPBuffer returns 0 on success and -1 on failure (confirmed by unit tests), not the recv size. HandleClient stores the return in r_sz and uses it as a length: the full-buffer guard (sb_size - r_sz) <= 2 never trips, and sb_size -= r_sz never shrinks. Chunks without newlines are strncat'd into storage_buffer[OS_MAXSTR+2] until the stack overflows. Requires remoted syslog+TCP with the attacker in allowed-ips.
findings.impact: Unauthenticated stack overflow in the forked syslog-TCP remoted child as the remoted user whenever syslog TCP collection is enabled and the source IP is allowed. Crash is certain; code execution is plausible and yields a foothold on the manager HIDS host.
findings.attack_path:
1. Operator configures remoted connection=syslog and protocol=tcp with allowed-ips covering the attacker (common for device log collection).
2. Attacker connects to the syslog TCP port.
3. Attacker sends repeated ~100-byte chunks with no newline.
4. HandleClient keeps strncat'ing; sb_size never decreases.
5. After ~62 chunks storage_buffer overflows → crash/RCE as ossec.
findings.remediation: Make OS_RecvTCPBuffer return the received length (or an out-parameter) and update HandleClient accordingly. Bound appends by remaining capacity from strlen(storage_buffer) versus sizeof(storage_buffer).
findings.poc_video_notes: No live syslog-TCP remoted lab. Local simulation of r_sz=0 + strncat of 100-byte chunks overflowed past OS_MAXSTR+2 at iteration 61. Unit test confirms OS_RecvTCPBuffer returns 0 on success.
